name: Oppidum Councils
description: Leading households and exchange specialists coordinate the larger enclosed settlements of southern Britain.
note: The burghers estate is an engine proxy for heterogeneous oppidum households and exchange specialists; this does not reconstruct a municipal constitution or make every enclosed site a town.

name: Przeworsk Smithing Households
description: Metalworking households connect Vistula and upper-Oder settlements through tools ornaments weapons and exchange.
note: Workshop and grave evidence supports metalworking and exchange but not a centralized craft guild; the burghers estate is a technical household-production proxy.

name: Dyakovo Hillfort Households
description: Household communities maintain defended promontory settlements along the upper Volga and Oka waterways.
note: Hillfort occupation and function varied; this is a bounded settlement adapter rather than evidence for one polity-wide defensive system.

name: Gorodets Rampart Custodians
description: Local households contribute labor and watch service to timber-and-earth defended settlements.
note: The privilege converts archaeological fortification evidence into gameplay without asserting permanent garrisons or a common constitution.

name: Northern Seasonal Rounds
description: Mobile households coordinate fishing hunting gathering and exchange between rivers lakes and the White Sea.
note: The round is an ecological gameplay abstraction across distinct northern material horizons and is not a claim of uniform ethnicity or subsistence.

name: Dnieper River Brokers
description: Exchange households mediate movement along the Dnieper Dvina Neman and their forest-steppe approaches.
note: The burghers estate is a technical proxy for exchange households; the privilege does not posit a unified river league or homogeneous trade system.

name: Kama Sanctuary Custodians
description: Ritual specialists and leading households maintain offering places tied to Kama and Vychegda communities.
note: Glyadenovo offering complexes support a ritual layer; the clergy estate remains a technical proxy and does not imply an organized priesthood across every frame.

name: Pyanobor Mortuary Households
description: Kin groups maintain local burial obligations and display regional metalwork within Kama exchange networks.
note: Mortuary assemblages support a household-memory mechanic but cannot establish one Pyanobor people polity or legal code.

name: Sargat Kurgan Retinues
description: Mounted and foot retainers gather around leading forest-steppe households whose status is displayed in kurgan cemeteries.
note: Variable kurgan wealth supports differentiated leading households but not one centralized Sargat aristocracy or standing army.

name: Altai Contact Caravans
description: Exchange brokers move horses metalwork and prestige goods between Altai valleys and the wider Inner Asian contact zone.
note: Contact goods do not establish Xiongnu occupation or a formal caravan institution; the privilege is a bounded exchange-network adapter.

name: Kulay Casting Households
description: Specialist households cast distinctive bronze objects within forest and river exchange networks.
note: The burghers estate is a technical specialist-production proxy; dispersed casting traditions are not treated as a guild or unitary Kulay polity.

name: Hillfort Retinues
description: Local fighting households maintain defended gathering places and answer the muster of their leading lineages.
note: Hillfort functions and occupation varied greatly; the privilege is a bounded military-political adapter rather than a claim that every polity had a permanent garrison.

name: Channel Exchange Compacts
description: Coastal households protect reciprocal exchange routes linking southern Britain with continental markets.
note: This represents cross-Channel exchange and elite brokerage without asserting a uniform customs regime merchant estate or Roman client treaty.

name: Cattle Compacts
description: Kin groups regulate seasonal herding obligations and the redistribution of livestock wealth.
note: This is a conservative pastoral gameplay adapter and does not project later written Irish law tracts or quantified herd systems into AD 1.

name: Maritime Followings
description: Coastal households provide crews for fishing exchange and opportunistic seaborne warfare.
note: Ptolemy supports an island ring of coastal peoples but not a uniform raiding institution; the privilege deliberately combines subsistence exchange and bounded military mobility.

name: Ritual Specialists
description: Local ritual experts mediate communal vows deposits and sacred obligations without a centralized hierarchy.
note: The clergy estate is a technical proxy for diverse ritual specialists; archaeological deposits do not establish a uniform druidic college or island-wide priesthood.

name: Assembly Acclamation
description: Free households and leading lineages voice assent at armed public gatherings.
note: Tacitus describes public deliberation but compresses diverse communities; this privilege models negotiated assent without inventing a uniform Germanic constitution.

name: Household Retainers
description: Leading households sustain sworn fighting companions through gifts hospitality and captured wealth.
note: The nobles estate is a technical proxy for unequal martial followings and does not imply feudal tenure hereditary peerage or one standardized comitatus.

name: Sacred Grove Custodians
description: Local ritual specialists guard communal groves vows and divinatory obligations.
note: Tacitus supports groves and divination but not a centralized priesthood; the clergy estate remains a bounded interface adapter.

name: Amber-Route Brokers
description: Coastal and riverine households mediate the collection exchange and southward movement of amber.
note: The burghers estate is a technical proxy for exchange households; no urban merchant corporation customs regime or unified Aestian state is implied.

name: Hillfort Households
description: Households maintain defended gathering places storage and seasonal community obligations.
note: Brushed Pottery hillfort evidence supports defended settlement systems but not one Baltic political constitution or permanent garrison.

name: Burial Custodians
description: Kin and ritual specialists preserve local barrow stone-circle and tarand mortuary obligations.
note: Material-culture boundaries and burial forms are gameplay frames rather than proof of fixed ethnic institutions or a shared priestly hierarchy.

name: Regional Satraps
description: Regional military and court elites mediate Indo-Scythian royal authority.
note: The nobles estate is a technical proxy for heterogeneous regional satrapal and military elites, not a uniform feudal order.

name: Hellenic City Elites
description: Urban elites sustain the last Indo-Greek royal court in the eastern Punjab.
note: The burghers estate is a technical proxy for urban and courtly elites and does not classify the late Indo-Greek polity as a medieval town republic.

name: Clan Assembly
description: Leading warrior clans participate in the council that governs the ganasangha.
note: The nobles estate is a technical proxy for the leading clans and does not equate a ganasangha with a European hereditary nobility.

name: Monastic Patronage
description: Royal endowments sustain Theravada monastic communities and irrigation works.
note: The clergy estate is a technical proxy for Buddhist monastic institutions and not a reconstruction of their exact fiscal or legal status.

name: Senatorial Land Exemption
description: Senatorial landed wealth receives protected fiscal treatment.
note: The nobles estate is a technical proxy for the senatorial aristocracy pending country-specific estate support.

name: Equestrian Service
description: The equestrian order supplies officers and civil administrators to the Augustan state.
note: The nobles estate is a technical proxy for Rome's second aristocratic order and does not merge equites with senators or recreate an exact office hierarchy.

name: Priestly Colleges
description: Pontifical and augural colleges safeguard the public ritual on which Roman state life depends.
note: The clergy estate is a technical proxy for public Roman priests and colleges rather than a Christian hierarchy or an exhaustive Roman cult constitution.

name: Annona
description: Public grain provision stabilizes Rome's urban population.
note: The burghers estate is a technical proxy for the urban plebs receiving the annona.

name: Praetorian Donatives
description: Regular donatives bind the imperial military household to the princeps.
note: The nobles estate is the documented technical fallback: the local estate registry has no safe country-specific attachment point; M10 owns the later legionary crisis interactions. The donative is an imperial hold on the guard so it contributes crown power rather than senatorial leverage. EU5 requires a power set on the attached estate so the small noble-power debit is that attachment rather than stacked senatorial grants.

name: Palace Bureau
description: Palace personnel and clerks provide a court-centred administrative channel.
note: The burghers estate is a technical proxy for a court-bureaucratic actor rather than a claim that eunuchs were burghers.

name: Wang Clan Regency
description: The Grand Empress Dowager entrusts governance to Wang Mang and his regency circle during Emperor Ping's minority.
note: The nobles estate is a technical proxy for the documented affinal-regency network rather than a claim that Wang kin formed a hereditary European-style estate or a complete Han constitution.

name: Great-House Autonomy
description: The great Iranian houses retain a substantial political role beside the Arsacid court.
note: The nobles estate represents the Suren and Karen type of great-house politics.

name: Client Royal Autonomy
description: A local royal court retains room to govern within an imperial patronage relationship.
note: The nobles estate is a technical proxy for the court elite of a Roman client kingdom.

name: Kushite Royal Court
description: A royal court sustains the authority of the Kushite co-rulers.
note: The nobles estate is a technical proxy for the court and temple-connected elite rather than a claim of a European-style nobility.

name: Clan Autonomy
description: The constituent clans retain decisive influence within the Xiongnu confederation.
note: The tribes estate directly represents constituent confederation groups rather than an invented settled aristocracy.

name: Early Korean Royal Court
description: Royal authority in Goguryeo is supported by its leading political houses.
note: The nobles estate is a technical court-elite proxy pending a dedicated early Korean institutional pass.

name: Elder Council
description: Leading kin groups constrain and sustain the ruler of a tribal kingdom.
note: The tribes estate is a technical representation of the leading kin groups rather than a complete reconstruction of Germanic or Brittonic assembly practice.

name: Druidic Councils
description: Druidic religious specialists advise leading kin groups in the pre-conquest Brittonic polities.
note: The clergy estate is a narrow technical proxy for religious specialists and not evidence for a single constitutional council across Britain or an inference about every Celtic society.

name: Sub-King Autonomy
description: A regional Iranian court retains substantial authority within the Arsacid political world.
note: The nobles estate is a technical regional-court proxy for Media Atropatene and must not be read as a uniform satrapal constitution.

name: Border-Court Autonomy
description: A frontier royal court balances local elites against stronger neighbouring powers.
note: The nobles estate is a technical proxy for a frontier court rather than a claim that Armenia and Osroene shared an institution.

name: Second Temple Priesthood
description: The Jerusalem priesthood retains religious and civic authority around the Temple.
note: The clergy estate is a technical proxy for the Temple priesthood and is not a claim of a Christian clerical hierarchy.

name: Regional Royal Court
description: Leading court figures support the authority of a regional monarch.
note: The nobles estate is a generic technical court-elite proxy and does not reconstruct a uniform ancient aristocracy.

name: Chiefly Court
description: Leading kin and local authorities sustain a developing chiefly polity.
note: The tribes estate is a technical proxy for chiefly authority and does not reconstruct an exact Aksumite political hierarchy.

name: Town-Cluster Council
description: Leading urban households coordinate the public life of a settled town cluster.
note: The burghers estate is a technical urban-community proxy and does not claim a documented Djenné-Djenno council constitution.
